policy: A model is listed only with an open licence, a pinned source revision and a SHA-256 for every file. Files are loaded from this site (/models/…) or chosen from the user's device, and are refused if a hash does not match. Research use only.

models.title: Biomedical entity recognition
models.summary: Tags 42 entity types in English clinical text: diseases and disorders, signs and symptoms, medications, dosages, diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, lab values, anatomy, durations and more.
models.architecture: DistilBERT (uncased, 66 M parameters), dynamic int8 quantisation; WordPiece tokenizer, up to 512 tokens per window
models.citation: Raza S, Reji DJ, Shajan F, Bashir SR. Large-scale application of named entity recognition to biomedicine and epidemiology. PLOS Digital Health 2022;1(12):e0000152.
models.trainingData: MACCROBAT2018: 200 annotated clinical case reports from PubMed Central (Caufield et al., figshare 2018).
models.evaluatedOn: No held-out accuracy evaluation is published with the model card, and Cerebro OS has not measured accuracy. What is checked (npm run test:models): on sample texts this browser runtime's token labels agree with the full-precision model as often as Python onnxruntime's int8 labels do (91–95% of tokens).
models.intendedUse: Research: highlighting candidate entities in case reports and abstracts for reading, screening and data extraction, with a human checking every result.
limitations: Trained on 200 case reports: expect missed and wrong entities, especially outside case-report style text.
English only; lower-cased input, so case distinctions (e.g. gene vs. protein names) are lost.
The weights are int8-quantised (67 MB instead of 266 MB): on sample texts 5–9% of word-piece labels differ from the full-precision model, so borderline entities can change between runtimes.
Some label names in the upstream configuration are malformed (e.g. 'Non[biological](Detailed_description'); they are shown as published.
Not a medical device and not for clinical decisions.
models.example: A 48 year-old female presented with vaginal bleeding and abnormal Pap smears. Upon diagnosis of invasive non-keratinizing SCC of the cervix, she underwent a radical hysterectomy with salpingo-oophorectomy which demonstrated positive spread to the pelvic lymph nodes and the parametrium.
